papers_read.title_as_printed: Explainable Machine Learning with Pairwise Interactions for Predicting Conversion from Mild Cognitive Impairment to Alzheimer's Disease Utilizing Multi-Modalities Data (Cai et al.; Brain Sci. 2023, 13, 1535)
A Graph Gaussian Embedding Method for Predicting Alzheimer's Disease Progression with MEG Brain Networks (Xu et al.; IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2021, 68(5):1579-1588) - NOT the paper the record means

Transfer learning for predicting conversion from mild cognitive impairment to dementia of Alzheimer's type based on a three-dimensional convolutional neural network (Bae et al.; Neurobiology of Aging 99 (2021) 53-64) - read as the source of the record's P-174 claim

what_each_reports.P-211: ADNI 1/2/3/GO, 1042 amnestic MCI at baseline; Explainable Boosting Machine on tabular baseline features (FreeSurfer hippocampal/amygdala/entorhinal/inferior temporal volumes and thickness, ADAS13, MMSE, FAQ, CDR-SB, age, sex, education, baseline EMCI/LMCI, APOE4), 5-fold CV. Five-year prediction: accuracy 85%, AUC 0.92 with MRI + cognitive scores (Comb a); only 225 participants remain at 5 years (140 MCI / 85 dementia). At three years the comb-a model with interactions gives accuracy 0.75, AUC 0.81 on the test data.
what_each_reports.P-174: The pack's PDF for P-174 is an MEG paper (Madrid cohort, 76 MCI + 53 controls, resting-state MEG graph embeddings): mean sMCI/pMCI accuracy 78% across ten classifiers; no ADNI data and no AUC of 0.827 anywhere in the text.
what_each_reports.P-37 (the record's P-174 claim): ADNI, 3D-CNN (ResNet29) pretrained on NC vs DAT and retrained on MCI-C (conversion within 3 years, n=228) vs MCI-NC (stable at least 3 years, n=222), single baseline sMRI scan; single held-out test set of 68: accuracy 82.4%, AUC 0.827.

quantity_a: AUC for MCI-to-AD conversion within 5 years, ADNI amnestic MCI, tabular MRI volumes plus cognitive scores, demographics and APOE4, 5-fold CV.
quantity_b: AUC for MCI-to-DAT conversion within 3 years (against MCI stable for at least 3 years), ADNI, whole-brain T1 sMRI images only, 3D-CNN with transfer learning, single held-out test split (n=68).
incompatible_if_same: No. At the matched three-year horizon P-211 itself reports AUC 0.81 on its test data, which is close to Bae et al.'s 0.827; the 0.92 is a five-year figure. Neither study evaluates the other's model or claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: match in label (both MCI-to-AD conversion, T2) but the horizons differ (5 years vs 3 years)
gates.dataset_family: match for the claimed P-174 content (ADNI in both); mismatch if the pack's MEG PDF were taken as P-174 (Madrid hospital cohort, not ADNI)
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal only (5-fold CV vs single random hold-out), V2
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-211 is tabular FreeSurfer measures plus neuropsychological scores and APOE4 (clinical/cognitive + sMRI-derived), P-37 is raw sMRI images only (the MEG PDF would be a third modality); the record itself sets modality_family_equal 'No'

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: same metric type (ROC AUC) but different prediction horizons (5-year vs 3-year conversion) and different predictor sets (cognitive scores dominate P-211's mid-term models; P-37 uses imaging alone).
performance_validity: flag does not apply: 0.92 and 0.827 are both below 0.97; not decisive here.
independence: Distinct author groups (Xi'an Jiaotong vs Northwestern/Simon Fraser); both use ADNI MCI participants and may overlap.
grounds: P-211's AUC 0.92 is for conversion within five years, whereas the record's P-174 figure (Bae et al., AUC 0.827) is for conversion within three years.
P-211 predicts from cognitive test scores, demographics, APOE4 and regional MRI volumes, whereas Bae et al. predict from the MRI image alone, so the predictor sets differ.
At the matched three-year horizon P-211 reports AUC 0.81, so no disagreement survives once the horizon is aligned.

The pack's P-174 PDF is the wrong paper (an MEG study); the claim was traced to Bae et al. (P-37 in the corpus, of which the P-174 block is a flagged duplicate stub), and the verdict is the same whichever of the two is read.

evidence_quotes.quote: The five-years prediction accuracy reached 85% (AUC = 0.92) using both cognitive scores and MRI markers.
The baseline information was used as input of all EBMs and the converting AD or not during follow-up period was used as output. All EBMs were tested with the 5-fold cross validation.
The main performance indicators, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC, were 0.75, 0.78, 0.73, and 0.81 (with interaction effects)
In the target task, we examined MCI-C patients with a conversion time of up to 3 years ... This resulted in 228 MCI-C patients and 222 MCI-NC patients.
It produced a test set classification accuracy of 82.4% and 0.827 area under the curve as well as 0.189 equal error rate value
MG2G achieved high performance with 61% for NC/sMCI/pMCI classification, 79% for NC/sMCI classification, 78% for sMCI/pMCI classification

record_defects: paper_b P-174 is a '[STUB-DEDUP-OF-P-171]' block that 'must not be cited as evidence'; its content (and the 0.827) is Bae et al. 2021, already P-37 in the corpus (P-171 was itself marked duplicate_of P-37 on 2026-09-27).
The PDF mapped to P-174 in the pack (MEG graph embedding, Xu et al.) is not the paper the record's claim comes from; the map entry is 'formula-unverified'.
claim_a 'AUC 0.92 on T2' omits that 0.92 is the five-year horizon (225 participants remaining); the three-year AUC is 0.81.
Registry Sample_N_Approx '242804' for P-211 is impossible; the paper has 1042 MCI participants.
resolution_note says 'Confirmed genuine' while resolution says 'Rejected: Task, dataset, or modality mismatch' and the status is partially_resolved_candidate: internally inconsistent.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A P-211 result at a three-year horizon that differed from 0.827 beyond both studies' uncertainty, with a matched predictor set; the paper's own three-year figure (0.81) does not.
